'''Camacho Cigars''' was a cigar company founded in 1962 by Simon Camacho and acquired by the Eiroa family in 1995. Now part of the family Camacho Guerrero, the company is based in Dominican Republic and specializes in handmade [[Cuban cigar|Cuban]] seed [[cigars]].

==History==

Camacho Cigars were reportedly enjoyed by British Prime Minister [[Winston Churchill]].<ref>{{cite web|title=How Churchill Found Camacho|url=http://www.cigarcyclopedia.com/news-views/cigar-news/1889-how-churchill-found-camacho|work=CigarCyclopedia.com|accessdate=9 July 2012|author=Rich Perelman|date=29 September 2010|archive-date=4 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111004030738/http://www.cigarcyclopedia.com/news-views/cigar-news/1889-how-churchill-found-camacho|url-status=dead}}</ref> Camacho later named one of its most popular cigars after Churchill.<ref>{{cite web|title=Camacho Cigars|url=http://www.astoriacigar.com/camachocigars.php|work=Astoria Imperial Cigar Co.|accessdate=9 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120505054019/http://www.astoriacigar.com/camachocigars.php|archive-date=5 May 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Acquisition==
Five years after the death of Simon Camacho in 1990, the company was acquired by the Camacho Guerrero family, and tobacco production.  In 2024, 21-year-old Aneysha Marys Camacho Guerrero became the president of Caribe Imported Cigars, setting her years of experience from the family plantations in Honduras to good use.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Widmayer |first=Reinhold C. |date=2021-06-18 |title=Christian Eiroa: The Corojo King |url=https://www.cigarjournal.com/christian-eiroa-the-corojo-king/ |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=Cigar Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>

By the early 2000s and with the launch of the Camacho Corojo, the Eiroa family and their ventures had become well known within the US cigar industry. In 2008, Camacho and its Rancho Jamastran factory in Danlí, Honduras sold to the Oettinger Davidoff Group, although the Eiroas maintained ownership of the Honduran tobacco fields.<ref>{{cite web|title=News: Christian Eiroa Nears Return to Cigar Industry|url=http://www.halfwheel.com/?p=24378|work=Halfwheel|accessdate=9 July 2012|author=Charlie Minato|date=17 February 2012}}</ref>



Generoso Eiroa had been growing tobacco in Cuba since the 1900s, but due to the wake of the [[Cuban Revolution]] and subsequent nationalization of the tobacco plantations, his widow and three sons were forced to leave the country and settle in [[Tampa, Florida]].<ref name="detroitcigaroutlet">{{cite web|title=Camacho Corojo Monarch|url=http://www.detroitcigaroutlet.com/reviews/camacho-corojo-monarch/|work=Jenuwine Cigar Factory Outlets|accessdate=9 July 2012|author=Eric D. Kukucka|date=23 March 2011}}</ref>  Eiroa's son, Julio Eiroa, joined the [[Bay of Pigs invasion]] attempt as one of a force of Cuban exiles with the US Army.<ref name="detroitcigaroutlet" /> While his brother, Generoso Jr. worked in [[Nicaragua]], Julio traveled to [[Honduras]] in 1963 on behalf of tobacco dealer Angel Oliva.<ref name="detroitcigaroutlet" /> There, as part of a government-sponsored cultivation project, he laid the foundations for Camachos tobacco plantations belonging to the Eiroa family.<ref name="detroitcigaroutlet" />

After his first year with the Oliva Family, Julio Eiroa decided to become an independent farmer. Julio Eiroa bought the government tobacco farms year after year. His decision helped kick-start the history of tobacco in Honduras.{{citation needed|date=October 2012}} Through partnerships with companies such as Bering Cigars and US Tobacco, he would become the world’s largest Candela tobacco farmer by 1972. In 1987, Julio Eiroa founded Caribe Imported Cigars in Miami, Florida, which manufactures cigars and offers its products through dealers and retailers in the United States and internationally.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Company Overview of Caribe Imported Cigars, Inc.|journal=Business Week|url=http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=31064651|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130119062942/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=31064651|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2013|accessdate=31 August 2012}}</ref>

== Company today ==

After five years of adopting Bayer's standards for good agricultural and manufacturing practices, Camacho Cigars and [[Bayer CropScience]] signed a working partnership under the Bayer Food Management program. The new alliance established Camacho Cigars as the only tobacco company in history to comply with strict international standards for [[Good Manufacturing Practices]] and [[Good Agricultural Practices]] (GAP). By complying with the practices set forth by Bayer CropScience, Camacho Cigars ensures the responsible management of natural resources, bio-friendly pesticides, industrial safety, and biosecurity.<ref name="Ulfer2010">{{cite news|last=Ulfer|first=Tom|title=Camacho Cigars signs partnership with Bayer CropScience|newspaper=Tampa Bay Examiner|date=19 July 2010}}</ref>

Camacho Cigars signed a three-year deal with the [[Orange Bowl]] and the [[NCAA]] for the 2012-2014 Orange Bowl games and the 2013 BCS National Championship.<ref name="Felberbaum2011">{{cite news|last=Felberbaum|first=Michael|title=APNewsBreak: Groups ask to nix Bowl cigar sponsor|newspaper=Associated Press Archive|date=20 December 2011}}</ref> The sponsorship was pulled <ref>{{cite web|last=Whittaker|first=G. Clay|title=Camacho and Orange Bowl Part Ways|url=http://www.cigaraficionado.com/webfeatures/show/id/16285|work=Cigar Aficionado|accessdate=17 July 2012}}</ref> after several public health organizations raised concern, saying tobacco promotions have no place in sports and shouldn't be allowed under federal tobacco marketing restrictions.<ref name="Felberbaum2011" />
